post.caption: A Renaissance necklace held a toothpick. In the 1500s, a decorated toothpick counted as a jewel. Men wore them on a chain around the neck. Makers used gold and enamel, then added pearls and rubies. In 1562, Erasmus Hornick published toothpick designs in Nuremberg. In the British Museum, a mermaid's body is one baroque pearl. In the Rijksmuseum, a gold dragon's tail is the toothpick. A Vienna pendant combines a toothpick with an ear spoon. Queen Elizabeth I received gold toothpicks as New Year's gifts. The Met keeps a gold ear pick from Roman times.
